The system we live in cannot last because it depends on endless growth, bad assumptions, and goals that don’t line up with reality. It tries to keep growing by replacing things that run out, but the replacements are weaker and cause more problems. This makes the system weak and unable to handle big changes, like running out of resources or damaging the environment.

The system doesn’t see its real problems, so the solutions it offers are fake and only make things worse. It believes technology can fix everything, but this belief hides the damage technology can also cause. Debt, war, and making things break on purpose are part of how it works, but they create even bigger problems in the long run. The system seems stable, but it’s actually full of weak spots that could fall apart at any moment.

It doesn’t have the tools or values to change in ways that would actually help. New groups of people who don’t fit into old political or social categories are showing up, but the system doesn’t know how to deal with them. It’s also full of people who know just enough to keep things going but not enough to fix or improve anything. Because the system is stuck and unable to change, the best option is for individuals to focus on small, personal ways to live differently, creating systems in their own lives that can handle the future better.

Gainesville does not typically have balanced political views because its population is heavily influenced by the presence of the University of Florida, which leans liberal. College towns tend to attract younger, more progressive residents, including students, faculty, and researchers who often favor left-leaning policies on education, healthcare, and social justice. This creates a strong liberal base that outweighs more conservative perspectives.  

However, outside the immediate university area, there are residents with more moderate or conservative views, especially in the suburbs and rural parts of Alachua County. These communities may prioritize issues like lower taxes, limited government, and traditional values, but their influence is smaller compared to the university population. This mix of urban liberalism and suburban conservatism can create some ideological diversity, though the balance is still skewed.  

Local elections and policy discussions often reflect the dominance of progressive ideas, with an emphasis on environmental sustainability, affordable housing, and public transportation. While conservative voices are present, they tend to have less political power due to the demographic and cultural makeup of Gainesville. This makes the city lean distinctly to the left, even if some political diversity exists within the broader region.

Fear grows when we imagine the worst, but most of it isn’t real and disappears when we face it. 

Desire promises happiness if we get something, but once we have it, we often want something else. 

What truly matters—like love, time, and health—is often ignored until we lose it.  

Instead of fearing, we can focus on what’s real and solve what we can. 

Instead of chasing things, we can find joy in what we already have. 

And instead of taking life for granted, we can treasure the people and moments that make it special.

An open heart is a way of being that welcomes others without judgment or fear. It means approaching people with kindness, curiosity, and the willingness to understand them as they are, not as we assume them to be. It is the courage to embrace vulnerability, allowing connections to form in their truest, most authentic form.

Success, to me, is a journey, an ongoing pursuit of harmony and connection with the deeper truths of the spiritual realm, all people we interact with, and the natural world around us. It involves not just the fulfillment of basic needs such as peace, privacy, food, clothing, and shelter, but also the ability to secure them in a way that allows us to focus on personal growth and understanding. 

True success, I believe, is reaching a point where we are not only self-sufficient but also generous, giving of ourselves to help others experience the same balance and security. By contributing to the well-being of those around us, we create a ripple effect that promotes shared understanding and a more harmonious existence for all.

In Paynes Prairie Preserve, a large natural area in Florida, there are wild pigs called feral hogs. These pigs dig up the ground with their snouts, looking for food like roots and insects, which can harm the environment by damaging plants and soil. To protect the park, workers set up special traps to catch these pigs. Once caught, the pigs are shot dead, then removed to a secluded area for vultures to devour. This helps keep the park's ecosystem healthy and safe for other animals and plants.

Food Not Bombs is a group of people who believe that no one should go hungry, especially when there is plenty of food in the world. They take food that stores and restaurants might throw away, like extra vegetables or bread, and cook meals to share with anyone who needs them. Instead of selling the food, they give it away for free because they believe food should be for everyone, not just for people who can pay for it.

This group started many years ago when some people saw that the government was spending a lot of money on war while many people had no food to eat. They wanted to show that helping people is more important than fighting wars, so they started making meals and giving them out in parks and city streets. Now, people all over the world do the same thing, cooking food together and sharing it with anyone who is hungry.
